newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ National MP Banks denies he'll quit parliament.
newsitem.headline: NZ National MP Banks denies he'll quit parliament.

text.p: National MP John Banks on Thursday rejected claims that he will quit parliament if the privileges committee clears Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters of a contempt of parliament charge.
Speaking on his Radio Pacific breakfast show Banks said he had no intention of walking away, and would remain in parliament to keep Peters and Prime Minister Jim Bolger honest.
"I'm not going to resign from parliament.
"I'm going to keep these two honest, that's what I'm going to do. That's a promise.
"I'm going to keep them honest, how could I keep them honest if walked away from parliament?"
The charge against Peters relate to a late night dispute between Peters and Banks in a parliamentary corridor. Peters denies allegations he assaulted Banks but has apologised for upsetting him.
It was speculated on Wednesday that Banks would quit if the committee cleared Peters of any wrong-doing.
Banks is MP for Whangarei and if he quit, a by-election would be required in his seat.
He won the seat by a few hundred votes from New Zealand First list MP Brian Donnelly last October with the Labour candidate a distant third.
The National/New Zealand First coalition government has a 61/59 majority at present.
A spokesman for Bolger said on Wednesday the government had received no ultimatum from Banks, but rumours that he might resign were being taken seriously.
"They have to be taken seriously but we have yet to establish whether Mr Banks is really making these noises."
Radio New Zealand reported on Thursday it had tried to get Banks on its Morning Report programme to discuss the claims but he declined.
However, Radio New Zealand said, Banks had told them rumours of his pending resignation were "pure fiction" and had no basis of fact.
